subtitle: Lesson 21 · Interoperability: Python + Q#

steps.label: A real repo layout for Q# plus Python
qsharp.json + src/ is the quantum library boundary
steps.sub: Independently compilable, testable, and resource-estimable — no Python required

steps.label: Python stays decoupled from implementation details
steps.sub: It only needs operation names and signatures, not how the oracle works

steps.label: A real gotcha: recompilation timing
steps.sub: Stale Python-side references can still point at the old compiled version

code:
my-quantum-project/
├── qsharp.json
├── src/
│   ├── Oracles.qs
│   ├── Diffusion.qs
│   └── Algorithms.qs
├── requirements.txt
├── experiments/
│   ├── run_grover_sweep.py
│   └── plot_results.py
└── notebooks/
    └── exploration.ipynb
caption: qsharp.json + src/ is the Q# project proper. experiments/ is Python that consumes it, like any other library.
Operations under src/ become available by their fully-qualified namespace name, same as an inline notebook cell.

steps.label: Editing a .qs file auto-recompiles
steps.sub: No manual "rebuild" step needed inside an active qsharp.init() session

steps.label: But stale Python references can linger
steps.sub: A variable holding an old compiled callable may not reflect the edit

steps.label: First thing to check
steps.sub: Re-run the Python call — don't assume the edit took effect everywhere
